title: Index Through the Array Twice
statement:
You get an array nums of length n that contains every number from 0 to n − 1 exactly once, in some order.

Return a new array out of the same length where out[i] = nums[nums[i]]: read the value at i, use it as an index, and read again.

examples.why: out[0] = nums[3] = 4, out[1] = nums[0] = 3, and so on. This is not the inverse permutation, which would be [1, 2, 4, 0, 3].
Each pair swaps places, and following a swap twice brings you back to where you started.
A single element points at itself.

constraints: nums is a permutation of 0 … n − 1
hints: The definition is already the algorithm. Which array do you read from: the original or the one you are building?
A fresh output array keeps the original values intact while you read them.
For O(1) extra space, store two numbers in one slot: nums[i] + n · (new value). Since every value is below n, % n recovers the old one and / n the new one.

explain.intuition:
With a separate output array this is one line: read nums[nums[i]] for every i. The point of the exercise is to notice why you need that separate array: if you overwrite nums[i] in place, a later j with nums[j] = i reads the new value instead of the original one.

The in-place trick avoids that by packing two values into one slot. Every value is in [0, n), so nums[i] + n · v keeps the old value in % n and the new value in ÷ n. In the first pass, always read through % n; in the second pass, divide.
steps: Return out. (In place: first add n · (nums[nums[i]] % n) to every slot, then replace each slot by floor(slot / n).)
pitfalls: Overwriting nums[i] directly, so later reads see changed values.
In the in-place version, reading nums[nums[i]] without % n after some slots were already encoded.
Confusing the result with the inverse permutation, where out[nums[i]] = i. They match only for special inputs like swaps, so check the first example.

complexity.space: O(n) for the output (O(1) extra in place)

solutions.title: Separate output array
solutions.idea: Read twice through the untouched input for every index.

solutions.title: In place with two values per slot
solutions.idea: Encode the new value as a multiple of n on top of the old one, then divide.

followups: Return the result of following the pointers k times, for k up to 10^9. (Think cycles, or repeated squaring.)
Do the in-place version without the multiplication trick, by walking each cycle of the permutation.
